stories.title: Java4Shell: RCE in OpenJDK when processing Base64
stories.blurb: AI-assisted security research firm Calif has uncovered a remote code execution vulnerability in OpenJDK triggered during Base64 processing — the second major language-runtime RCE they've found in weeks. With Java underpinning huge swathes of enterprise infrastructure, this is patch-now territory. The 308-comment HN thread is worth reading for scope and mitigation details.

stories.title: Quad9's withdrawal from France: A canary in the coal mine
stories.blurb: Cloudflare's analysis of Quad9 being forced out of France by DNS-level piracy blocking legislation is a sharp warning about how privacy-respecting DNS resolvers are being weaponised as censorship chokepoints. The implications for privacy infrastructure globally are significant — and the 400-comment debate is one of the liveliest on HN today.

stories.title: AI is killing All About Berlin
stories.blurb: The creator of a beloved Berlin expat resource documents how AI-generated summaries and answer engines have gutted his traffic and, with it, his ability to maintain the site. A raw, first-person account of the information-ecosystem damage done when LLMs consume niche human expertise without attribution or compensation. The most-commented story on HN today.

stories.title: Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%
stories.blurb: Data-backed analysis showing Google's AI Overviews have clawed back roughly 40% of outbound search clicks — confirming what many webmasters feared. If you run any kind of content property or rely on search-driven discovery, this is the new baseline to plan around.

stories.title: ID.me terms required for IRS sign-in
stories.blurb: The IRS now funnels taxpayers through ID.me's facial-recognition and data-brokering terms as a mandatory step for account access. Consumer-rights advocates have documented the specific problematic clauses — this is a privacy red flag that affects every American filing taxes online.

stories.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: 385x more efficient inference
stories.blurb: Researchers propose a fundamentally different inference architecture that replaces autoregressive token prediction with energy minimisation, claiming 385× efficiency gains on reasoning tasks. If the numbers hold up under scrutiny, this could reshape the economics of running reasoning models locally — very relevant for anyone building AI-assisted workflows.

stories.title: Pre-auth RCE in Nginx HTTP/2 handling
stories.blurb: Wiz's security team has detailed a pre-authentication remote code execution vulnerability in Nginx's HTTP/2 stack — no credentials needed to compromise a server. Nginx powers a huge fraction of the web; check your versions and patch immediately.

stories.title: Why is Gemini 4 Carbon taking so long?
stories.blurb: A well-sourced technical post unpacking the engineering and supply-chain bottlenecks delaying Google's next flagship model. Understanding the competitive dynamics here matters if you're making tooling bets — Anthropic and OpenAI are benefiting from every month of delay.

stories.title: A Perfect SimCity
stories.blurb: An obsessive deep dive into achieving a mathematically optimal SimCity 1 city — complete with algorithmic analysis and tool-assisted play. It's part retrocomputing love letter, part constraint-satisfaction puzzle, and entirely delightful.

stories.title: Claude was trained on protein sequences at scale
stories.blurb: A researcher's findings that Claude Opus was trained on large-scale protein sequence data, surfacing unexpected cross-domain reasoning capabilities. This has real implications for how we think about emergent skills in large language models — and for anyone using Claude in scientific or biotech contexts.

stories.title: Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop | Claude by Anthropic
stories.blurb: Anthropic's official guidance on agent architecture decisions — specifically when a subagent abstraction adds value versus when it creates unnecessary complexity. Essential reading for Claude Code users building multi-step agentic workflows.

stories.title: I fix vibe-coded apps for a living, and they all have the same problems
stories.blurb: A developer who professionally debugs AI-generated codebases identifies four recurring failure patterns. If you're using Claude Code or any coding assistant to ship production software, this is the checklist you need before you hand off.

stories.title: The nature of my job has completely changed
stories.blurb: A developer's candid reflection on how agentic coding tools have shifted their role from writer of code to reviewer and director of AI output. It's a nuanced take — neither utopian nor dismissive — on what day-to-day work actually feels like now.

stories.title: Catching AI's mistakes is a mental burden – and a drag on productivity
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: ai, verification, burden, skill-swap
stories.blurb: Cognitive scientists put a name to the hidden cost of AI tools: the 'verification burden' — the mental overhead of double-checking outputs that partially offsets productivity gains. The 1985 'responsibility-authority double bind' framing is sharp and directly applicable to anyone using AI coding assistants.

stories.title: OpenCode | Browse, your real browser for coding agents
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: web, tools, ai, agents
stories.blurb: OpenCode's Browse product gives coding agents an actual browser with full JS execution rather than a headless scraper — meaning agents can interact with SPAs, auth flows, and dynamic pages like a real user would. A meaningful upgrade for any agentic workflow that needs to navigate the modern web.

stories.title: Clipen – Clipboard Manager for Mac with Clipboard History
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: macos, clipboard, manager, app
stories.blurb: A new macOS clipboard manager focused on a clean UI and persistent clipboard history. For heavy Obsidian and coding workflows where you're constantly juggling snippets, a solid clipboard manager is table-stakes productivity infrastructure.

stories.title: Search Browser — a fast, light web browser for the Mac
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: macos, web, browser
stories.blurb: A purpose-built macOS browser optimised for search and research workflows rather than general browsing — think keyboard-first navigation and fast retrieval. Worth a look for developers who live in documentation and want something lighter than Chrome or Firefox.

stories.title: Ductus · Your handwriting, as a font
stories.blurb: Draw your letters directly in the browser and download a fully-formed OTF/WOFF2 font — no account, no upload, everything processed locally on your device. Privacy-respecting and genuinely fun; great for personalising Obsidian notes or creative projects.

stories.title: CutWire Drift — Free CapCut Alternative
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: video, editing, app, editor
stories.blurb: An open-source, cross-platform video editor with a multi-track timeline, auto-captions, effects, and cutouts — no subscription, no watermark, no account required. A timely CapCut replacement for anyone who wants full creative control without the data-harvesting baggage.

stories.title: How Rust Changed Me As A Developer
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: rust, programming, architecture, bestpractices
stories.blurb: A thoughtful essay on how writing Rust rewires your instincts about ownership, error handling, and API design — lessons that transfer back into any language you pick up afterwards. The architecture and best-practices angle makes it relevant even if you never ship a Rust crate.
